seat_pm.HG-20211028-046885-S: PRE-MORTEM (before the call, from the sheet): a SHORT at 4.4375 eighty-four seconds into the NY phase, on a session ALREADY +$1,268.75 that has spent **89.5% of its expected move with $315.80 of statistical room left — less than a third of the $1,000 bar.** THE CONTENT IS GOOD: S5 trades/min 54 at z=4.85 with slope -$81.25/min and accel -61.3; S8 60s -21 on 85 and phase -11 on 109 with 75 of 109 contracts above the mid; 4 of 4 through-book prints clearing the BID; S7 refill 0.489 with a 10.9ms median restore (a fast, thin book); S10 in_VA=1, d_POC -$62.50 (at value). THE DEATH MECHANISM: **the arithmetic.** For this seat to pay $1,000 the day must break its own expected range by three times what remains, in a phase that opened 85 seconds ago on a tape whose 30-minute flow is flat (+10 on 575). The give-back version is worse: a fast thin book with a 10ms restore is exactly the tape that snaps back through a short. THE TRIGGER: a print above 4.4433 (the 13:00:01 phase H) kills it; if the mid is still between 4.4360 and 4.4433 at 15:00 the seat is dead by exhaustion and the wall never binds.
seat_pm.SI-20211028-046915-L: PRE-MORTEM (auto, triage): the opposite-side twin — a LONG in SI at the same minute with every flow window buying and 77 of 80 phase contracts below the mid, in_VA=1 with d_POC +$87.50, on a session with $1,589 of expected move unspent. If both seats pay, the metals were not one bet today and my day-1/2/5 complaint about correlated seats is regime-specific; if both die, the correlation was in the CLOCK, not the direction. Either way today prices that question. TRIGGER: a print below 24.13 (the 13:00:35 phase L).

novel.HG-20211028-046885-S: novel (day 7): **THE OPPOSITE-SIDE SAME-MINUTE PAIR.** HG/NY SHORT 13:01:25 and SI/NY LONG 13:01:55 — same generator family, same clock, same in_VA=1 geometry, opposite sides, both admitted by the same five terms.
